trust_decision.summary: Bytes passed to safe Rules::deserialize are decoded by bincode and trusted as-is: index/ID fields (SubPatternId, code locations) and literal-pool UTF-8 are later used in unchecked/unsafe operations during scanning and metadata access, with no post-decode validation.

landing_point.why: Summary names `Rules::deserialize`; an engineer reads this function first and sees it returns bincode output with no validation.

fix_sites.entry_point: Rules::deserialize / Rules::deserialize_from (Rust API), yrx_rules_deserialize (C API, capi/src/rules.rs:118), Python Rules.deserialize_from (py/src/lib.rs:1295), CLI `yr scan --compiled-rules` (cli/src/commands/scan.rs:242)
none directly; derive Ord on SubPatternId to support .max() in the rules.rs check
Rule::metadata() iterator (public Rust API, reached by CLI/C/Python metadata output)
fix_sites.module_kind: public model/accessor layer, separate from deserializer

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/src/models.rs:208 (Metadata iterator: unsafe to_str_unchecked on lit_pool bytes; the UTF-8 invariant is only established at compile time, not by the deserializer at lib/src/string_pool.rs:255-259)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report points at deserialize/scanning; the metadata accessor is a read-only model API in another module whose comment asserts the string is 'sure' to be valid UTF-8, so a solver can argue it is not reachable by the deserialization bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Round-trip of legitimately compiled rules (serialize -> deserialize -> scan) must keep working, including rules with no atoms (empty atoms vector) and rules whose sub-patterns are anchored-only or chained; an over-strict check (e.g. requiring atoms non-empty, or rejecting the native compiled_wasm_mod path) breaks them. Metadata strings that are valid UTF-8 must still be returned as MetaValue::String, not Bytes/error.

O6_input_shapes: MetaValue::String literal id pointing at non-UTF-8 bytes in lit_pool

O7_producer.where: lib/src/compiler/rules.rs:51 (#[derive(Deserialize)] on Rules) plus custom pool deserializers lib/src/string_pool.rs:220-259; the invariants are produced by the compiler (Compiler::build), which deserialize never calls

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: IDs nested inside SubPattern enum values (chain heads/tails) rather than top-level index vectors; chains look like a neighbouring feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: scanner module; field defined in lib/src/compiler/mod.rs:2998-3012

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Looks like the upstream fix; a solver copying its shape inherits the bug.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Regex code locations (FwdCodeLoc/BckCodeLoc in SubPattern) index deserialized re_code, decoded with get_unchecked in PikeVM/InstrParser
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Regex VM is a separate engine package (re/thompson); bytecode validity reads as a compiler invariant, not deserializer scope.

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: native-code-serialization is an opt-in feature and the fix's own new doc says untrusted blobs are unsupported.
